props.text: #185: afkv2 verification: propose-verification (medium lane) + small lane, highest-value test level with proof

## Pain

An agent added a clickable Jira ticket URL to a lavish page, declared the job done, and the link did not work. The agent never ran the changed behavior through its real entry point. Nothing in afkv2 made it.

## Goal

Verification runs automatically in every development task: a small bug fix, a small enhancement, a full feature. Anything testable is tested, with proof, at the highest-value level at minimum:

- testable through a UI → test it through the UI;
- testable through an API → test the API;
- testable at contract level → contract (Pact) test.

The bigger the task, the more levels of tests (unit to UAT).

## Scope

1. **Medium lane — `/afkv2:propose-verification`**: port v1 `grill-verification` in the afkv2 lean spirit (remove frictions and blockers, instructions over scripts). Agents research, investigate, multi-provider proposers draft and debate, then propose a final verification plan. The human sees the full plan, high to low level, on the lavish page and steers it — no grilling form. The plan is executed in subtasks during development and at the end before ship.
2. **Small lane**: bring the half-built v1 small lane (branch `feat/feat-small-lane`, `docs/afk/small-lane/`) to v2 in the same spirit. Human and agents still talk through the issue, the expected fix and how to test it, even if only for a few minutes.

## Evidence found (round 0)

- v1 chain: grill-verification → VERIFICATION-PLAN.md → to-subtasks smoke gate → smoke-test. Script-gated; no highest-value-level rule; no contract (Pact) testing.
- v1 small lane: bugs only; diagnose/fix split with approval; proof = failing-then-passing test, all tiers, live before/after. 6 of 13 subtasks done; two review stalemates.
- afkv2 (`feat/afkv2`): medium lane only; `propose-verification` planned for P1 and small lane for 2.1 (`docs/afk/afkv2/PRD.md`); the autopilot done check verifies the TDD verdict and Produces anchors but never records Verification rows; `not applicable:` accepts any reason; no feature-level gate; change-request proofs are unchecked free text.

items.title: How the proof rule is made to hold

props.text:
My definition. Accept or correct it.

**Highest-value level**: the level closest to how a user meets the change. In order: UI > API > contract > integration > unit.

- "At minimum" means the proof must reach that level. Lower-level tests add to it; they never replace it.
- A UI is any surface a person uses: a web page, a terminal command, a skill run in a real session. For this plugin, a page change is proved by opening the page in a browser and clicking; a skill change by running the skill.
- A change with no user-visible effect (a refactor) goes to its highest reachable level: often integration or unit, plus proof that existing behavior did not change.

items.title: What "highest-value level" means

props.text:
My definition. Accept or correct it.

**Testable at a level**: the agent can reach that level here and now: the app starts, a browser tool exists, the credentials exist.

When the highest level is out of reach, the agent never drops it silently:

1. It says what is missing: app not running, no browser, no test account.
2. It fixes what it safely can: starts the app, opens the browser tool.
3. Otherwise it asks you to supply it, or to accept a lower level. Your answer goes on the change.

A hands-off executor cannot ask, so it parks the subtask, as today.

This replaces `not applicable: <any reason>` for live levels.

**Counter-question:** what does this block? A level that cannot run on a laptop (for example only on staging). Recovery: you accept the lower level, or point the agent at staging.
